# Database schema (`navaid_db`)

> Part of the reference docs. See [`README.md`](../README.md) for the index.

Extensions: `postgis`, `pgrouting`.

```
--- Routable network (generated by osm2pgrouting) ------------------
ways
  gid BIGSERIAL PK, osm_id BIGINT,
  source BIGINT, target BIGINT,                  [idx on both]
  length_m DOUBLE PRECISION,
  the_geom GEOMETRY(LineString, 4326)            [GiST]
  -- tag columns retained from the OSM import:
  covered BOOLEAN, is_steps BOOLEAN,
  crossing_kind TEXT,        -- 'signals' | 'marked' | 'unmarked' | NULL
  wheelchair TEXT, surface TEXT, incline NUMERIC

ways_vertices_pgr
  id BIGSERIAL PK, the_geom GEOMETRY(Point, 4326) [GiST],
  branch_count INT,          -- degree of the vertex, cached at import
  decision_cost DOUBLE PRECISION   -- derived, see 05-methodology.md

way_profile_cost                      (1 row per way per profile)
  way_gid BIGINT FK -> ways(gid),
  profile TEXT,              -- 'euclidean' | 'default' | 'limited'
  cost DOUBLE PRECISION,     -- seconds, with penalties applied
  reverse_cost DOUBLE PRECISION
  PRIMARY KEY (way_gid, profile)

  Precomputed at import so routing is a plain cost column lookup rather
  than a CASE expression evaluated per query.

--- Landmarks -----------------------------------------------------
landmarks
  id SERIAL PK,
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL,        -- 'gtp' | 'mrt_exit' | 'bus_stop'
                             -- | 'clinic' | 'caregiver' | 'route_derived'
  source_ref TEXT,           -- postal code, stop code, exit code, etc.
  description TEXT,          -- what the walker would recognise
  colour TEXT, motif TEXT,   -- for murals and signage
  salience SMALLINT,         -- 1-5, see 05-methodology.md
  visibility_m INT,          -- approximate range it can be seen from
  planning_area_id INT FK -> planning_areas(id),
  nearest_vertex BIGINT FK -> ways_vertices_pgr(id),   [idx]
  geom GEOMETRY(Point, 4326) NOT NULL                  [GiST]

  nearest_vertex is resolved at import. A landmark matters relative to a
  decision point, not as a free-floating coordinate.

go_to_points                          (destination attributes for kind='gtp')
  landmark_id INT PK FK -> landmarks(id),
  address TEXT, postal_code TEXT,
  hours_raw TEXT,            -- the DESCRIPTION field, unparsed
  hours_parsed JSONB,        -- best-effort parse, NULL where unparseable
  phone TEXT,
  tenant_names TEXT[],       -- rows collapsed into this building
  last_updated DATE

--- User data -----------------------------------------------------
saved_destinations
  id SERIAL PK,
  label TEXT NOT NULL,       -- 'home', 'Auntie May', spoken by the user
  aliases TEXT[],            -- alternate phrasings the parser may see
  geom GEOMETRY(Point, 4326) NOT NULL,
  nearest_vertex BIGINT FK -> ways_vertices_pgr(id)

recorded_routes
  id SERIAL PK,
  destination_id INT FK -> saved_destinations(id),
  recorded_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  way_gids BIGINT[]          -- ordered, the path actually walked

  Segments appearing here are discounted by the familiarity term. A known
  path is preferred over a shorter unknown one.

--- Study area and evaluation -------------------------------------
planning_areas
  id SERIAL PK, name TEXT UNIQUE, region TEXT,
  geom GEOMETRY(MultiPolygon, 4326)              [GiST]

  Study-area filter only. Carries no analytical weight.

gps_traces                            (evaluation data, not runtime)
  id SERIAL PK,
  route_id INT,              -- the computed route being verified
  walked_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  geom GEOMETRY(LineString, 4326),
  accuracy_m NUMERIC[]       -- per-fix accuracy as reported by the browser
```

## Notes

`nearest_vertex` on `landmarks` and `saved_destinations` is resolved once at
import rather than per query. Snapping to a graph vertex also absorbs a few
metres of positional error, which matters because Go-To Point coordinates are
building-level and caregiver entries are phone-GPS-level.

`way_profile_cost` is a separate table rather than columns on `ways` so that
adding a profile does not require a schema migration, and so the `euclidean`
baseline can be stored alongside the walking profiles for direct comparison.

`gps_traces` exists for the field verification in `05-methodology.md`. It is
not read by the running application and can be dropped in a deployment.

Regenerate with `python import_osm.py && python import_data.py` — see
[`01-setup.md`](01-setup.md).
